In Malawi, empty #pesticide containers are punctured to prevent others from reusing them (e.g. water storage). 

However, highly concentrated residues from pesticide #packaging and the #plastic itself can still leak into water and soils, which poses serious environmental and human health risks.

Unfortunately, this plastic often has nowhere to go.

In the current linear economy, the cost and burden of disposal is generally passed onto the consumer – but safe disposal and #recycling systems for plastic waste are underdeveloped and often inaccessible.

name: member-pzlu
text:
As a chair of Global Health Engineering, we not only work on global sanitation and health problems. Our Master student, Dominic Wälti, investigates and evaluates working conditions of the crew at Entsorgung + Recycling Zürich (ERZ) with the dual purpose of improving these conditions and developing practical technological solutions to reduce physical strain. His research focuses on waste collection sites spread throughout the city of Zurich. It turns out that a recurring problem emerges where waste is not handled properly, according to regulations. As a result, a significant amount of waste ends up being deposited on the ground. This issue requires the workforce to address the unauthorized disposal. The workers bear the responsibility of manually cleaning the collection sites, they take on this demanding task without the aid of specialized tools or equipment.
 
Dominic's cross-disciplinary thesis encompasses systematic assessment of health at work and technical solution development. Ergonomic analysis methodologies are used for the investigation of physical exertion. Risk assessment tools are applied within this context. Dominic spent two weeks with the workers to observe and assess their working routine, as well as interview them to get insightful suggestions for health at work improvement. His final results are the recommendations provided to ERZ.

February 2024 was the warmest February on record with a global surface air temperature 1.77°C above the 1850-1900 pre-industrial average. January 2024 was the warmest January on record, along with every single month since June of 2023. The previous months are consequently surpassing the 1.5 °C goal of the Paris Agreement. Switzerland has committed to halving its greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 and reaching net zero by 2050, partly through emission offsetting in other countries, with a goal of offsetting over a million tonnes of CO2-equivalent until 2030. Only the relevant technology allows for emission offsetting and only the relevant technology allows for accurate emission estimation.

Currenlty, five of our students develop solutions to reliably and inexpensively estimate the emissions offset by the biogas reactors and improved cookstoves, both interesting and important for the Swiss policy makers.

One of the most touching ❤️ moments during the closing workshop of our research project "Climate risk, land loss, and migration: Evidence from a Quasi-Experiment in Bangladesh" 🇧🇩 was when one of our study participants shared the story of her family who had repeatedly lost their house 🏠 and land due to riverbank erosion and a lack of government support. With her story, she challenged the high-level representatives of international and government organizations who had previously presented their strategies for climate change adaptation in Bangladesh. 
This situation vividly illustrates the gap that we frequently experience between what governmental and international organizations plan, and what the communities on the ground would actually want or need. If we are serious about effective climate change adaptation, we urgently need to close this gap. 
What are your experiences? Have you witnessed a similar misalignment between community needs and government plans in other settings?

This powerful tool streamlines the transcription of audio files while also performing speaker diarization, meaning it identifies and separates who is speaking when. It uses cutting-edge open-source models – 𝗙𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗪𝗵𝗶𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗿 and 𝗣𝘆𝗮𝗻𝗻𝗼𝘁𝗲 – to obtain the best possible results.

Crucially, 𝚐𝚑𝚎_𝚝𝚛𝚊𝚗𝚜𝚌𝚛𝚒𝚋𝚎 helps 𝗿𝗲𝗺𝗼𝘃𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗸 𝗼𝗳 𝗹𝗲𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗳𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝗶𝗻𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗼 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝗿𝗱 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗶𝗲𝘀. 🔒 You have the flexibility to run it locally on your machine, ensuring your sensitive data stays secure. For those working with larger audio files or wanting to avoid slowing down their local computer, we've also provided clear instructions to run it directly on the 𝗘𝘂𝗹𝗲𝗿 𝗰𝗹𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿, which is open to all ETH members. 💻

𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗰𝗵𝗼𝗼𝘀𝗲 𝚐𝚑𝚎_𝚝𝚛𝚊𝚗𝚜𝚌𝚛𝚒𝚋𝚎 𝗮𝘁 𝗘𝗧𝗛? 🤔 Because we're actively collaborating with IT services here to bring you an even more seamless experience! We're working towards providing a fast, one-click access to the tool directly from your browser window on Euler's JupyterHUB instance – 𝗻𝗼 𝗶𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗿𝗲𝗾𝘂𝗶𝗿𝗲𝗱! 🤯

But that's not all! ✨ 𝚐𝚑𝚎_𝚝𝚛𝚊𝚗𝚜𝚌𝚛𝚒𝚋𝚎 has been specifically designed with 𝗙𝗔𝗜𝗥 𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗮 𝗣𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗲𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗤𝘂𝗮𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗥𝗲𝘀𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗰𝗵 𝗶𝗻 𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗱𝗶𝘀𝗰𝗶𝗽𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆 in mind, aligning perfectly with the goals of the FAIRqual project. 💪 We believe in making research data Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable, and this package is a significant step towards achieving that for qualitative data in collaborative, transdisciplinary settings.

♻️ Procrastinating your trip to the recycling point? A new planning workflow combines GIS and MILP to improve access to Sammelstellen in Zurich and beyond.
Environmental Sciences Master’s thesis student @Silas Schweizer developed an urban planning workflow combining GIS and Mixed-Integer Linear Programming to improve @Entsorgung + Recycling Zurich’s glass and metal recycling network.
🔍 His analysis focusing on pedestrian access and network constraints recommends 12 new collection points, reducing:
- the number of underserved residents by 9’000
- average walking time to recycling points by 20 seconds
👏 A great example of using data to improve recycling rates and helping reach emissions reductions targets. 

🖥️ Code & data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15320179
📖 Publication coming soon!
#Recycling #GIS #UrbanPlanning #ETHZurich #SmartCities #StudentSuccess

How do smallholder farmers in Malawi 🇲🇼 use biogas?

Thanks to a consistent supply of nutrient-rich effluent, farmers now planning to plant 🌽 multiple times annually to boost their harvests which is important given that around half of Malawi's population is affected by food insecurity. Moreover, having access to biogas also allows farmers to cook indoors without smoke, eliminating a significant source of air pollution.  Natalie Alice Boyd Williams's research was supported by the ever wonderful Stella Chisenga [ON LINKEDIN], Owen Mtambo [ON LINKEDIN], and Cyrus Lloyd [NO LINKEDIN].

text:
🌍 Advancing Open Research Data (ORD) Practices: Collaboration & Innovation in the ETH Domain

Last week, Elizabeth Tilley and Lars Schöbitz had the opportunity to share experiences with Project FAIRqual at the ETH Board Open Research Data conference. 🤝 

This collaborative project brings together Global Health Engineering's expertise in open data practices with the innovative research approaches of  Franziska Mohr, Mollie Chapman, and Bianca Vienni-Baptista from the Department of Environmental Systems Science (D-USYS), ETH Zürich D-Transdisciplinarity Lab, focusing on FAIR Data Practices for Qualitative Research in Transdisciplinarity. 🔬✨

We discussed four critical challenge areas when sharing qualitative data:

- 🔒 Practical issues around confidentiality and data heterogeneity 
- 🤫 Ethical commitments to participant trust 
- 🧠 Epistemological traditions that value embodied research presence 
- 📊 The predominantly quantitative origins of current open science frameworks

The FAIRqual project represents our commitment to advancing open research practices while respecting the unique requirements of qualitative research. 🌱 We’re collaboratively developing new approaches that honor both open science principles and methodological integrity, creating pathways for more inclusive research practices. 🌐

💡 Explore our full presentation: https://fairqual.org/gallery/slides/

#OpenScience #QualitativeResearch #FAIR #Transdisciplinarity #OpenData

name: member-zt6s
text:
Want to learn about plastic bag recycling? 🔄 Six weeks ago, @Elizabeth Tilley, Thalia Laios, @Padraic Casserly and @Waste Advisors interns visited Green Pak near Blantyre, Malawi 🇲🇼 - and captured this fascinating transformation process on video.

Watch plastic waste become woven bags through mechanical recycling: collection & sorting → shredding into flakes → melt extrusion (yes, "spaghettified"  🍝 into molten strands!) → film formation → weaving into durable fabric. 

Malawi's plastic crisis: The country produces 75,000 tonnes of plastic annually, with 80% being single-use and non-recyclable (UNDP/Turpie et al., 2019). More critically, an estimated 28,000-32,000 tonnes of mismanaged plastic waste enters the environment each year due to a 42% waste collection rate (UNDP, 2019).

Why this matters : Facilities like Green Pak provide alternatives to the 15 (!) currently operating plastic manufacturing companies in Malawi (UNDP/Turpie et al., 2019). Each woven bag represents approximately 50-100 discarded items diverted from Lake Malawi and urban drainage systems.

Have you seen similar initiatives tackling plastic waste in your region?

name: member-f4ib
text:
At ETH Zurich’s Global Health Engineering group, we’ve developed a new biogas monitoring sensor that measures gas flow, methane concentration, pressure, and temperature in household biodigesters. With a solar-powered communication module, it delivers real-time, reliable data on how much biogas is produced and used.

Why does this matter? For smallholder farmers, biodigesters aren’t just clean energy systems—they also unlock carbon crediting, where reduced emissions can be verified and sold to generate income. But in Kenya (and much of Africa), crediting often relies on proxy data and assumptions, creating uncertainty and undervaluing impact.

That’s where our sensor comes in. By piloting it in Kenya with St. Paul’s University, we aim to:
✅ Strengthen carbon credit verification
✅ Boost trust in carbon markets
✅ Unlock fairer financing for farmers
✅ Provide insights to improve biodigester performance

Kenya’s vibrant carbon market ecosystem makes it the perfect place to start. This pilot is just the first step, but it could transform how household biogas systems are measured and valued—locally and globally.

💡 We’re excited to see where this leads and to keep building bridges between technology, climate action, and livelihoods.

text:
📢 Air quality in Blantyre, Malawi!

We measured black carbon (BC)—a pollutant harmful to 🌍 climate and 🫁 health.

💨 Average concentrations were 3.85 µg/m³ in the dry winter months, comparable to bigger sub-Saharan African cities. With Blantyre still urbanizing, pollution could worsen without action. 

🚫 Unfortunately, there are no regulatory standards for ambient BC concentrations—despite its health and climate impacts—raising questions about what levels are safe and highlighting the need for both research and regulation.

✨ This is the first study in Malawi to identify BC sources, using locally determined AAE values to distinguish fossil fuel from biomass burning.

📖 Read our paper: https://lnkd.in/gsHq3sUt

👥 Authors: @Saloni Vijay, @Hope Kelvin Chilunga, @Lars Schöbitz & @Elizabeth Tilley

text:
Last Friday, Lars Schöbitz participated in the 4th Annual Meeting of the Swiss Reproducibility Network. One of the many highlights was the talk by Katrin Milzow of the Swiss National Science Foundation SNSF Research Development Department.

Katrin noted that the SNSF has identified important gaps and the need to move beyond focusing solely on the submission of Data Management Plans to must-have FAIR and open digital research objects. In her presentation, she outlined three key levers to reinforce FAIR practices throughout the grant life cycle.

A “consideration by the evaluation body” for the proposal or project plan is an approach we thoroughly support.

National ORD Action Plan (see D1.2): https://openresearchdata.swiss/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/EPFL_ORD_ActionPlanV1.0_December_2021_def.pdf
